steps: Your 2–3 a.m. waking and night sweats

sections.title: What I’m hearing
sections.body: Eight months of 2–3 a.m. waking, occasional night sweats, fatigue, brain fog, changing periods, and 15 pounds of weight gain.

sections.title: The hypothalamic connection
sections.body: The hypothalamus helps regulate temperature and sleep. Deborah calls it the “maestro” of the hormonal symphony. Your symptoms alone can’t tell us exactly what is happening with it.

sections.title: What this may mean
sections.body: Perimenopause may be part of the picture. Poor sleep and your thyroid history are also worth discussing with your provider.

sections.title: Questions and tests worth discussing
sections.body: Ask whether your thyroid treatment needs review and whether any testing would help. Your provider can decide which tests are useful for you.

sections.title: What you can do now
sections.body: Track your sleep, night sweats, periods, and energy for your appointment. Aim to give yourself a longer sleep window when possible.

sections.title: Recommended next steps
sections.body: Book a provider visit to review these symptoms. Keep taking levothyroxine as prescribed unless your prescriber changes it.

sections.title: A word from Deborah
sections.body: “You’re noticing a pattern, and it deserves a closer look. You don’t have to figure out every piece before asking for help.”

sections.title: 1. Chief complaint
sections.body: “I’m exhausted and gaining weight no matter what I eat. I can’t think straight at work.” Sandra reports waking around 2–3 a.m. for eight months. She sometimes wakes drenched in sweat and estimates 15 pounds of weight gain over the past year.

sections.title: 2. Clinical context
body: Periods are still occurring but have become less predictable.
Walks 30 minutes, about three times a week.
Her doctor has said her thyroid is “fine,” but Sandra remains concerned about her symptoms.
Perimenopause was discussed as a possibility, not established as the cause.

sections.title: 3. Tests to discuss
sections.body: No specific tests were agreed on in the chat. Sandra can ask whether her thyroid treatment and recent thyroid results need review, and whether any further evaluation would help explain the fatigue and night sweats.

sections.title: 4. Questions for my provider
body: Could perimenopause be contributing to my changing periods, night sweats, and sleep problems?
Should we review my levothyroxine treatment and thyroid results?
Could disrupted sleep be contributing to my fatigue and brain fog?
Is any additional evaluation useful for the weight gain and night sweats?

sections.title: 6. Red flags & recommendation
sections.body: Sandra denied fever and unexplained weight loss when asked. This was a brief chat, not a complete medical assessment.
